title: Kids Story for Sleep: The Little Dormouse and the Sleepy Meadow 🐭🌙
logline: A wide-awake little dormouse takes a gentle moonlit walk through the meadow and, softly and slowly, finds his way to sleep.
theme: a bedtime adventure under the stars
moral: Calm comes softly when we breathe slow and let the day drift away.

characters.name: Pip
characters.description: A tiny, gentle dormouse, about four years old in dormouse years. Curious and sweet, but tonight he simply cannot fall asleep. Soft, sleepy voice.
characters.visual_description: a very small round dormouse with soft cinnamon-brown fur, a cream tummy, big sleepy amber eyes, and a pale blue knitted nightcap that keeps slipping down over one ear

characters.name: Mama Dormouse
characters.description: Pip's warm, patient mother. Calm and reassuring, never in a hurry. A voice like a soft blanket.
characters.visual_description: a soft grey-brown dormouse with kind half-closed eyes and a cozy cream shawl wrapped around her shoulders

characters.name: Bramble
characters.description: A drowsy old rabbit who greets everyone with an enormous yawn and shares the trick of slow breathing.
characters.visual_description: a plump, sleepy grey rabbit with very long floppy ears that droop, and a little patch of white fur on his chest

characters.name: Nyla
characters.description: A slow, gentle snail who carries a tiny dewdrop lantern and teaches Pip to go slower than slow.
characters.visual_description: a small garden snail with a swirled amber-and-cream shell that glows faintly, carrying a tiny glowing dewdrop lantern on a curled leaf

characters.name: Mother Nightingale
characters.description: A soft-voiced bird humming a wordless lullaby to her sleeping babies beneath her wing.
characters.visual_description: a small round nightingale with soft russet-brown feathers and a pale speckled chest, one wing tucked gently over three tiny sleeping chicks

story_text: The sky over Willow Meadow was turning soft and violet, the color of a cozy dream. One by one, the little lights of evening blinked awake — first one star, then two, then too many to count. In a snug burrow beneath the old willow tree, a tiny dormouse named Pip was wide, wide awake. Pip had a warm little bed of moss and feathers. Pip had a soft blue nightcap that slipped down over one ear. Pip had everything a sleepy dormouse could want... except the sleepy part. "Mama," Pip whispered, "my eyes just won't stay closed." Mama Dormouse smiled and gathered Pip close, her fur as warm as sunshine left over from the day. "Then let's go and visit the Sleepy Meadow," she said softly. "It always knows how to help." So out they went, into the hush of the evening, where the grass was cool and the air smelled of clover and rain. The moon hung low and round, like a friendly lantern watching over everything. They walked slowly. There was no hurry at all. Soon they came to Bramble the rabbit, sitting by his door with his long ears drooping. He opened his mouth in the biggest, widest yawn Pip had ever seen — a yawn so big it made Pip's own mouth open too. "Good evening, little Pip," Bramble said sleepily. "Can't sleep? Try this. Breathe in, slow as the rising moon..." He breathed in. "...and out, soft as the falling leaves." He breathed out. Pip breathed in, slow as the rising moon. And out, soft as the falling leaves. And Pip felt just a little bit sleepier. They said goodnight to Bramble and wandered on, past the silver stream that giggled quietly over its stones. There, gliding along a dewy leaf, was Nyla the snail, carrying a tiny lantern that glowed like a single drop of morning. "Hello, Pip," Nyla whispered. "Where are you off to, so late?" "I'm trying to find my sleep," said Pip. "Ah," said Nyla, smiling her slow, kind smile. "When I want to feel calm, I go slow. Slower than slow. I feel my heart go thump... thump... thump, like a soft little drum. Try it. There's no race to win." So Pip stood very still and felt the quiet thump of his own small heart. Thump... thump... thump. And Pip felt a little bit sleepier still. On they went, softer than a whisper, until they reached the hawthorn tree where Mother Nightingale sat with her babies tucked beneath her wing. She was humming — a low, gentle tune with no words, the kind of song that feels like being rocked. "Would you like to rest here a moment?" she hummed. Pip nestled into the warm grass and listened. The song rose and fell, rose and fell, like slow waves on a sleepy shore. Above, the stars twinkled — one, two, three... Pip tried to count them, but they were so many, and so soft, and so far away. Somewhere around star number nine, Pip's eyes grew heavy as two little pebbles. "Mama," Pip mumbled, "I think... the Sleepy Meadow is working." Mama Dormouse lifted Pip gently and carried him home beneath the watching moon. Pip's head rested on her shoulder, and his nightcap slipped down over one ear, and the whole meadow seemed to breathe slow and calm around them. Back in the snug burrow, Pip snuggled into his bed of moss and feathers. It was warm. It was soft. It was exactly right. "Breathe in, slow as the rising moon," Pip whispered to himself. "And out, soft as the falling leaves." Outside, the stars kept their quiet watch. The stream hummed its little song. Bramble slept, and Nyla slept, and Mother Nightingale tucked her wing a little closer. And in his cozy bed, beneath the old willow tree, little Pip closed his eyes at last... and drifted off into the softest, warmest, happiest dream. Goodnight, Pip. Goodnight, meadow. Goodnight, moon. Sleep well. Sleep deep. Sleep tight.
